newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight volatile, ends lower on liquidity.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight volatile, ends lower on liquidity.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate ended a volatile session at 6.5/7.0 percent against 7.5/8.0 percent previously as liquidity improved and demand eased towards the close, dealers said on Thursday.
They said the overnight hit a high of 8.6/7 percent in mid-afternoon trading before lending by some large local and foreign banks eased the pressure.
Dealers said the market was thin and many were still on holiday after the Chinese Lunar New Year and Moslem Eid al-Fitr festivals earlier this week.
"It is just an unpredictable market. Your cannot really say this is a trend because there is so little activity," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
In the morning, other interbank rates were mostly unchanged, also due to thin activity, the dealers said.
They said a holiday mood continued to prevail over the market after a five-day closure of banks from February 7 to 11.
They said the one-week interbank rate was at 7.50/60 percent, two-week was at 7.40/50 percent and one-month at 7.30/35 and six-month at 7.35/40 percent, all unchanged from Wednesday.

"The market should return to normal next week when everybody comes back to work and funds which had gone out during the festivals should also return to the system," said the head of money dealing at a Malaysian bank.
He said interest rates were expected to ease slightly as funds return to the system over the next two weeks.
An estimated three billion ringgit has temporarily left the banking system, mostly in cash, for the festivals.
